reason: In the BEFORE hunk the comparator returns 1 whenever `a` is either wildcard, so for a pair of wildcard keys (`.*` vs `(?:|/.*)`, which can be siblings for route sets like `/a*` plus `/a/*`) compare(a,b) and compare(b,a) both say "greater", leaving their relative order to sort-stability/insertion order — exactly the ambiguity the AFTER code removes by explicitly placing `.*` before the tail wildcard, confirming the alternation order (and thus which route wins) was previously not pinned.
